what: Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3, int8 ONNX export, on CPU
evidence: NOT evidence for this project. ASR targets a cloud GPU, so these numbers describe hardware that will not serve a request: they are a correctness check, not a latency result. Do not quote them in the report. The figure with a use beyond this file is load.per_process_ms, which decides whether engine construction has to leave the async lifespan.

settings.preprocessor: numpy (onnx-asr picks it when the first provider is CPU; nemo128.onnx is fetched anyway so a CUDA process can start offline)

load.note: Download excluded - paid once per machine. This is the cost of a process start, and the lifespan runs once per WebSocket test, not once per suite.
load.projected_suite_note: Only paid if the suite is run with ASR_MODEL=parakeet. It runs with ASR_MODEL=stub, which loads nothing.
load.async_lifespan_decision: init_engines() stays synchronous. Its docstring sets the trigger for wrapping the call site in to_thread.run_sync at 30-90 s of blocking load; both real stages together cost ~1 s here, which stalls no startup probe and no SIGTERM. Re-measure on the target GPU - a CUDA execution provider builds its context at session creation and is the case that could cross the threshold.

transcribe.note: Median over a warm session. The first call is slower because ONNX Runtime allocates its arenas on it.

broken_input_probe.why: Run deliberately, because the failure mode of this layer is silent: the VAD returns ~0 for every frame without its context window, and the MT decoder runs away without its terminator. Neither raises. The question was which wrong input this stage answers wrongly but plausibly.

unscaled_int16.input: raw int16 sample values cast to float32, never divided by full scale
unscaled_int16.finding: IDENTICAL to the correct output. The mel preprocessor normalizes amplitude away, so this scaling is not load-bearing for this model. It only emits a RuntimeWarning about an overflowing cast. A test guarding it would guard nothing.

garbage_float32.input: the WAV's byte payload reinterpreted as float32
garbage_float32.finding: 120 repeated <unk> with no separators. A word count does not catch it - the whole run splits as one token - so the opt-in test asserts on content words and bounds output length in CHARACTERS.
